demand_drivers.body:
- Tea is a seasonal, rain-dependent agricultural crop; yield depends heavily on weather conditions, irrigation and soil management.
- Erratic weather conditions, climate-change-induced shifts in monsoon patterns, and shortage of labour are flagged as main threats to the industry.
- Government/Tea Board promotional and brand-building initiatives, including TRUSTEA programmes, are expected to benefit the industry long term.
- Rising demand for packaged tea varieties with natural ingredients, and consumer preference shifting toward premium and health/wellness-focused teas, are cited as demand …

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Tea is totally a rain-dependent crop; erratic weather and climate-change-induced shifts in monsoon patterns (long dry spells followed by short heavy rain) directly affect crop yield despite technological advancement.
- Labour shortage, especially during peak season in some pockets, is flagged as a main threat; the tea industry is highly labour intensive.
- Increased supply in the global tea market and a slowdown in economic growth may adversely affect the Company's business prospects.
- Tea manufacture is seasonal (mid-March to mid-December) and crop yield depends heavily on irrigation, soil management and pest protection, all subject to management's continuous monitoring.
- Management must constantly monitor risks tied to changing market conditions and trends affecting the plantation and tea trade business.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Improving crop yield and quality through better irrigation facilities, soil management and use of vermi compost.
- Adopted Integrated Pest and Nutrient Management practices on the estates as part of an improvement drive.
- Made substantial investment in irrigation to minimize the impact of climatic change on crop.
- Carried out a restructuring exercise at key management level to improve plantation activities and overall corporate performance.
